import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Handle NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' by filling them with 'No Disorder'
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep
# Differentiate points by 'Sleep Disorder' using color (hue)
# Use 'Stress Level' to vary the size of the points, indicating its impact
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    size='Stress Level',
    sizes=(50, 600),  # Define the range of marker sizes for stress levels
    alpha=0.7,        # Set transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    palette='viridis' # Choose a distinct color palette
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Quality, Disorder, and Stress Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Rating)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlap with the plot
plt.legend(title='Sleep Disorder', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Add grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Adjust layout to make sure everything fits without overlapping
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Handle NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' by filling them with 'No Disorder'
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('No Disorder')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize the relationship between Sleep Duration and Quality of Sleep
# Differentiate points by 'Sleep Disorder' using color (hue)
# Use 'Stress Level' to vary the size of the points, indicating its impact
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    size='Stress Level',
    sizes=(50, 600),  # Define the range of marker sizes for stress levels
    alpha=0.7,        # Set transparency for better visibility of overlapping points
    palette='viridis' # Choose a distinct color palette
)

# Add title and labels for clarity
plt.title('Relationship Between Sleep Duration, Quality, Disorder, and Stress Level', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10 Rating)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlap with the plot
plt.legend(title='Sleep Disorder', bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0)

# Add grid for easier reading of values
plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
